(* 2026-10-15 ET. Prospective trusted heap semantics, not an admitted theorem.
   There are no source-specific propositions or recursive equations here.
   Allocation identities are mathematical integers, never machine epochs.
   Imported int.Int arithmetic is a separately inventoried trusted foundation.
*)
module Heap
  use int.Int
  use map.Map

  type cell = Integer int | Pointer int int
  type heap = {
    next : int;
    allocated : map int bool;
    alive : map int bool;
    dynamic : map int bool;
    writable : map int bool;
    extent : map int int;
    address : map int int;
    memory : map int (map int cell);
    initialized : map int (map int bool)
  }

  (* A concrete empty heap used only to prove feasibility of source entries.
     Arbitrary incoming heaps in member obligations remain quantified. *)
  function empty (dummy:int) : heap =
    { next = 1; allocated = (fun _ -> False); alive = (fun _ -> False);
      dynamic = (fun _ -> False); writable = (fun _ -> False);
      extent = (fun _ -> 0); address = (fun _ -> 0);
      memory = (fun _ -> (fun _ -> Integer 0));
      initialized = (fun _ -> (fun _ -> False)) }

  predicate live (h:heap) (b:int) = b <> 0 /\ h.alive[b] = True
  predicate issued (h:heap) (b:int) = h.allocated[b] = True
  predicate separated (h:heap) (b c:int) =
    h.address[b] + h.extent[b] <= h.address[c] \/
    h.address[c] + h.extent[c] <= h.address[b]
  predicate aligned (p alignment:int) = exists q:int. p = alignment*q
  predicate well_formed (h:heap) =
    0 < h.next /\
    (forall b:int. issued h b -> 0 < b < h.next) /\
    (forall b:int. live h b ->
      issued h b /\ 0 <= h.extent[b] /\ 0 < h.address[b]) /\
    (forall b,c:int. live h b /\ live h c /\ b <> c ->
      h.address[b] <> h.address[c] /\ separated h b c)

  (* Allocator output relation from the existing fresh-allocation policy.
     This is a uniform semantic primitive, not a new constructor precondition.
     Incoming receiver/buffer subobjects may overlap within one identity. *)
  predicate available (h:heap) (n a:int) =
    0 <= n /\ 0 < a /\ aligned a 4 /\
    (forall b:int. live h b ->
      a <> h.address[b] /\
      (a + 4*n <= h.address[b] \/ h.address[b] + h.extent[b] <= a))

  function fresh_id (h:heap) : int = h.next
  function bytes (h:heap) (b:int) : int = h.extent[b]
  function numerical_address (h:heap) (b:int) : int = h.address[b]
  predicate same_object (before after:heap) (b:int) =
    before.allocated[b] = after.allocated[b] /\
    before.alive[b] = after.alive[b] /\
    before.dynamic[b] = after.dynamic[b] /\
    before.writable[b] = after.writable[b] /\
    before.extent[b] = after.extent[b] /\
    before.address[b] = after.address[b]
  function contents (h:heap) (b o:int) : cell = h.memory[b][o]
  predicate initialized_at (h:heap) (b o:int) = h.initialized[b][o] = True
  predicate integer_at (h:heap) (b o v:int) = contents h b o = Integer v
  predicate pointer_at (h:heap) (b o target offset:int) =
    contents h b o = Pointer target offset
  predicate forms (h:heap) (b o:int) =
    live h b /\ 0 <= o <= h.extent[b]
  predicate can_read (h:heap) (b o width:int) =
    live h b /\ 0 <= o /\ 0 < width /\ o + width <= h.extent[b]
  predicate can_write (h:heap) (b o width:int) =
    can_read h b o width /\ h.writable[b] = True
  predicate typed_reads (h:heap) (b o width alignment:int) =
    can_read h b o width /\ aligned (h.address[b]+o) alignment
  predicate typed_writes (h:heap) (b o width alignment:int) =
    can_write h b o width /\ aligned (h.address[b]+o) alignment
  predicate typed_forms (h:heap) (b o alignment:int) =
    forms h b o /\ aligned (h.address[b]+o) alignment
  predicate freeable (h:heap) (b o:int) =
    live h b /\ h.dynamic[b] = True /\ o = 0

  (* Uniform allocator primitive. Fresh cells are uninitialized, not filled.
     Address is separate from identity, so reuse never revives an old alias. *)
  function allocate (h:heap) (n a:int) : heap =
    { h with next = h.next + 1;
      allocated = set h.allocated h.next True;
      alive = set h.alive h.next True;
      dynamic = set h.dynamic h.next True;
      writable = set h.writable h.next True;
      extent = set h.extent h.next (4*n);
      address = set h.address h.next a;
      initialized = set h.initialized h.next (fun _ -> False) }

  (* Uniform typed stores. Access checks are separate mapped obligations,
     never pre-proven by these total transition functions. *)
  function put_integer (h:heap) (b o v:int) : heap =
    { h with memory = set h.memory b (set h.memory[b] o (Integer v));
      initialized = set h.initialized b (set h.initialized[b] o True) }
  function put_pointer (h:heap) (b o target offset:int) : heap =
    { h with memory = set h.memory b (set h.memory[b] o (Pointer target offset));
      initialized = set h.initialized b (set h.initialized[b] o True) }

  (* No field reset and no alias rewriting. The null identity is zero. *)
  function release (h:heap) (b:int) : heap =
    if b = 0 then h else { h with alive = set h.alive b False }

  predicate filled_prefix (h:heap) (b k v:int) =
    forall j:int. 0 <= j < k ->
      initialized_at h b (4*j) /\ integer_at h b (4*j) v

  (* 2026-10-16 ET. Source-int embedding, not a new C caller requires.
     Only initialized typed int objects map to Integer cells in range. Pointer
     cells, padding, partial bytes and type-punned objects are not admitted by
     this relation. Every evaluated load has a separate access/type VC. *)
  function load_int (h:heap) (b o:int) : int =
    match contents h b o with
    | Integer v -> v
    | Pointer _ _ -> 0
    end

  predicate int32_at (h:heap) (b o:int) =
    typed_reads h b o 4 4 /\ initialized_at h b o /\
    integer_at h b o (load_int h b o) /\
    -2147483648 <= load_int h b o <= 2147483647
  predicate int32_region (h:heap) (b offset count:int) =
    forall j:int. 0 <= j < count -> int32_at h b (offset+4*j)

  (* Logical image construction from WP Typed's integer chunk, not a C store.
     Machine-range/source-object admission is checked separately. This does
     not assert that old initialized Pointer-tag cells were integer objects. *)
  type int_values = map int int
  function int_chunk_value (values:int_values) (offset:int) : int = values[offset]
  predicate int_slot (offset count p:int) =
    exists j:int. 0 <= j < count /\ p = offset+4*j
  predicate bounded_int_values (values:int_values) (offset count:int) =
    forall j:int. 0 <= j < count ->
      -2147483648 <= values[offset+4*j] <= 2147483647
  function project_int_region (h:heap) (values:int_values) (b offset count:int) : heap =
    { h with memory = set h.memory b
      (fun p -> if int_slot offset count p then Integer values[p] else h.memory[b][p]) }

  (* The entry snapshot contains arbitrary index-specific int values. The
     source stays live/unchanged until release; no uniformly filled input law
     or desired copy theorem is assumed. *)
  function copy_int (h:heap) (source source_offset target target_offset:int) : heap =
    put_integer h target target_offset (load_int h source source_offset)
  predicate copied_prefix (entry now:heap) (source source_offset target count:int) =
    forall j:int. 0 <= j < count ->
      int32_at now target (4*j) /\
      load_int now target (4*j) = load_int entry source (source_offset+4*j)

  (* Source automatic-object placement is a distinct semantic output relation.
     It ranges over arbitrary incoming heaps and unbounded fresh identities;
     no finite pool, epoch limit, dynamic-free permission or empty-heap premise.
     The caller map must bind the actual declaration/cleanup and target layout. *)
  predicate automatic_available (h:heap) (width alignment a:int) =
    0 <= width /\ 0 < a /\ 0 < alignment /\ aligned a alignment /\
    (forall b:int. live h b -> a <> h.address[b] /\
      (a+width <= h.address[b] \/ h.address[b]+h.extent[b] <= a))
  function begin_automatic (h:heap) (width a:int) : heap =
    { h with next = h.next+1;
      allocated = set h.allocated h.next True;
      alive = set h.alive h.next True;
      dynamic = set h.dynamic h.next False;
      writable = set h.writable h.next True;
      extent = set h.extent h.next width;
      address = set h.address h.next a;
      initialized = set h.initialized h.next (fun _ -> False) }
  function end_automatic (h:heap) (b:int) : heap = release h b
end
swdb/proof_report.ml:
(* Fresh-run inventory of ALL generated WP obligations, including never-tried goals.
   Created: 2026-10-15 ET (Probata ticket36). No consolidated Valid status
   establishes a proof. Individual Wpo results and generated IDs are independent
   of WP's report JSON (which omits untried goals). Extern is read separately. *)
open Frama_c_kernel

let esc s =
  let b = Buffer.create 80 in
  String.iter (function
    | '"' -> Buffer.add_string b "\\\""
    | '\\' -> Buffer.add_string b "\\\\"
    | '\n' -> Buffer.add_string b "\\n"
    | '\r' -> Buffer.add_string b "\\r"
    | '\t' -> Buffer.add_string b "\\t"
    | c when Char.code c < 32 -> Buffer.add_string b (Printf.sprintf "\\u%04x" (Char.code c))
    | c -> Buffer.add_char b c) s;
  "\"" ^ Buffer.contents b ^ "\""

let function_of p = match Property.get_kf p with
  | None -> "null" | Some kf -> esc (Kernel_function.get_name kf)
let loc p =
  let a, _ = Property.location p in
  Filepath.to_string_abs (Filepos.path a), Filepos.line a
let verdict = function
  | Wp.VCS.NoResult -> "untried" | Unknown -> "unknown" | Timeout -> "timeout"
  | Stepout -> "stepout" | Computing _ -> "computing" | Valid -> "valid"
  | Invalid -> "invalid" | Failed -> "failed"
let bool b = if b then "true" else "false"

let is_system p =
  let file, _ = loc p in
  String.starts_with
    ~prefix:(Filepath.to_string_abs (Kernel.Share.get_dir "libc")) file

let dependencies p =
  Property_status.fold_on_statuses
    (fun e _ acc -> List.rev_append e.Property_status.properties acc) p []

let run () = match Sys.getenv_opt "SWDB_PROOF_REPORT_OUT" with
  | None -> ()
  | Some path ->
    (* Status iteration alone is not a property census. -wp-status-all can
       bypass the lookup which lazily registers synthetic smoke IPOther values.
       Snapshot registered objects; union actual Wpo references without asking
       the status API to register those missing properties. 2026-10-16 ET. *)
    let registered = ref Property.Set.empty in
    let registered_order = ref [] in
    Property_status.iter (fun p ->
        registered := Property.Set.add p !registered;
        registered_order := p :: !registered_order);
    let references = ref [] in
    let smoke_properties = ref Property.Set.empty in
    let goals = ref [] in
    Wp.Wpo.iter_on_goals (fun w ->
        let p = Wp.Wpo.get_property w in
        references := p :: !references;
        if Wp.Wpo.is_smoke_test w then
          smoke_properties := Property.Set.add p !smoke_properties;
        let _, line = loc p in
        let doomed = Wp.WpPropId.doomed_if_valid w.Wp.Wpo.po_pid in
        references := List.rev_append doomed !references;
        let targets = List.map (fun p -> esc (Property.Names.get_prop_name_id p))
            doomed in
        let best = List.map (fun (_, (r : Wp.VCS.result)) -> verdict r.verdict) (Wp.Wpo.get_results w) in
        goals := Printf.sprintf
            "{\"goal\":%s,\"property\":%s,\"function\":%s,\"line\":%d,\"smoke\":%s,\"passed\":%s,\"targets\":[%s],\"results\":[%s]}"
            (esc (Wp.Wpo.get_gid w)) (esc (Property.Names.get_prop_name_id p))
            (function_of p) line (bool (Wp.Wpo.is_smoke_test w)) (bool (Wp.Wpo.is_passed w))
            (String.concat "," targets) (String.concat "," (List.map esc best)) :: !goals);
    let exported = ref Property.Set.empty in
    let pending = Queue.create () in
    let order = ref [] in
    let include_property p =
      if not (Property.Set.mem p !exported) then begin
        exported := Property.Set.add p !exported;
        Queue.add p pending;
        order := p :: !order
      end in
    List.iter (fun p -> if not (is_system p) then include_property p)
      (List.rev !registered_order);
    List.iter include_property (List.rev !references);
    while not (Queue.is_empty pending) do
      let p = Queue.take pending in
      List.iter include_property (dependencies p);
      match p with
      | Property.IPPropertyInstance instance -> include_property instance.ii_ip
      | _ -> ()
    done;
    let unregistered_smokes = ref [] in
    let names = Hashtbl.create 401 in
    let properties = ref [] in
    List.iter (fun p ->
          let _, line = loc p in
          let name = Property.Names.get_prop_name_id p in
          if Hashtbl.mem names name then failwith "duplicate exported property identity";
          Hashtbl.add names name ();
          let is_registered = Property.Set.mem p !registered in
          let extern =
            if is_registered then
              Property_status.Feedback.get p = Property_status.Feedback.Considered_valid
            else match p with
              | Property.IPOther other
                when Property.Set.mem p !smoke_properties &&
                     String.starts_with ~prefix:"wp_smoke_" other.io_name ->
                (* A live WP smoke reference, no registered/emitted status.
                   Do not call Feedback.get: its lazy status lookup would
                   register this IPOther. No assumption is introduced. *)
                if dependencies p <> [] then
                  failwith "unregistered smoke unexpectedly has status dependencies";
                unregistered_smokes := esc name :: !unregistered_smokes;
                false
              | _ -> failwith "unclassified unregistered property reference" in
          let emitter_name = match p with
            | Property.IPCodeAnnot ca -> Emitter.get_name (Annotations.emitter_of_code_annot ca.ica_ca ca.ica_stmt)
            | _ -> "" in
          let smoke_failure = match p with
            | Property.IPCodeAnnot ca ->
              let e = Annotations.emitter_of_code_annot ca.ica_ca ca.ica_stmt in
              let name = Emitter.get_name e in
              (match ca.ica_ca.annot_content with
               | Cil_types.AAssert (_, tp) ->
                 (String.starts_with ~prefix:"Wp" name || name = "Unreachable Annotations") && tp.tp_statement.pred_name = ["Wp"; "SmokeTest"]
               | _ -> false)
            | _ -> false in
          let dependencies = List.map Property.Names.get_prop_name_id (dependencies p) in
          let dependencies = List.sort_uniq String.compare dependencies in
          let origin = match p with
            | Property.IPPropertyInstance instance -> esc (Property.Names.get_prop_name_id instance.ii_ip)
            | _ -> "null" in
          let kind = match p with
            | Property.IPPredicate _ -> "contract"
            | Property.IPAssigns _ | Property.IPAllocation _ | Property.IPFrom _ -> "contract"
            | Property.IPDecrease _ -> "termination"
            | Property.IPLemma _ -> "lemma"
            | _ -> "other" in
          properties := Printf.sprintf
              "{\"property\":%s,\"function\":%s,\"kind\":%s,\"emitter\":%s,\"origin\":%s,\"dependencies\":[%s],\"extern\":%s,\"generated_smoke_failure\":%s,\"line\":%d,\"description\":%s,\"status_registered\":%s,\"property_export_origin\":%s}"
              (esc name) (function_of p) (esc kind) (esc emitter_name) origin (String.concat "," (List.map esc dependencies)) (bool extern) (bool smoke_failure) line
              (esc (Format.asprintf "%a" Property.pretty p)) (bool is_registered)
              (esc (if is_registered then "registered" else "wp-smoke-reference")) :: !properties)
      (List.rev !order);
    let oc = open_out path in
    Printf.fprintf oc "{\"version\":\"1\",\"goals\":[%s],\"properties\":[%s],\"complete\":true,\"property_closure\":{\"registered_snapshot_count\":%d,\"exported_count\":%d,\"unregistered_wp_smoke_properties\":[%s],\"unregistered_status_lookup_performed\":false}}\n"
      (String.concat "," (List.rev !goals)) (String.concat "," (List.rev !properties))
      (Property.Set.cardinal !registered) (Property.Set.cardinal !exported)
      (String.concat "," (List.rev !unregistered_smokes));
    close_out oc
let () = Boot.Main.extend run

"""The `std::vector<T>` and `std::pair<A, B>` models: a C struct per type plus one C function per member, each
with an ACSL contract citing the C++ standard's clause for it.

Created: 2026-10-14 ET (Probata proof of concept ticket 25). Design: formal-verification map 16 items 6 and 7
(`std::vector<T>` (not `bool`) and `std::pair` as modeled types; growth frees the old buffer; `at` out of range
is a proof obligation; new assumption entries), 11 item 11 (undefined behavior is a proof obligation).
Format: docs/reference/format-v0.4-std-models.md.

- Modeled, never lowered from libc++: the C lowering tool (`swdb.c_lowering`) turns each use of a modeled member
  into a call of its C function here, so no verifier ever runs libc++ internals.
- Citations name clauses of ISO/IEC 14882:2017 (C++17), the `-std` the C lowering parses with: `[vector.cons]`,
  `[vector.capacity]`, `[vector.data]`, `[vector.modifiers]`, `[vector.special]`, `[sequence.reqmts]`,
  `[container.requirements.general]`, `[stmt.ranged]` and `[pairs.pair]`.
- What the standard leaves to the implementation (the growth policy: when `capacity()` grows and by how much)
  follows the pinned libc++ 22.1.8 (`__recommend`: twice the capacity, at least the new size; `reserve(n)` and a
  copy allocate exactly), so a counterexample on the C lowering replays on the C++. A contract states only what
  the standard says: reallocation happens exactly when the new size exceeds the old capacity, and then the old
  buffer is no longer valid (stated through `\\valid` in `ensures`, 20's allowed-ACSL rules), so CBMC detects a stale pointer
  or iterator. WP refuses units with releases pending sound lifetime support.
- `at(n)` with `n >= size()` throws `std::out_of_range`; exceptions are outside the subset, so the contract makes
  `n < size()` the caller's obligation, and the C body calls `SWDB_MODEL_FAIL` (CBMC: a failed assertion; the
  native harness: a failed check; standalone: `abort()`, what an uncaught exception does). `operator[]` with
  `n >= size()` is undefined behavior: its contract requires `n < size()` and the body calls
  `SWDB_MODEL_REQUIRE` (CBMC: an assertion; native: nothing).
- Elements are scalars (integers, floating point) or pointers; `std::vector<bool>` and class elements are
  outside the model. Iterators are pointers (libc++'s `__wrap_iter<T *>` wraps one).
- Allocation succeeds (an assumption entry of every record that uses a model that allocates): the bodies call
  `swdb_alloc_<t>` and `swdb_free`. For WP (`__FRAMAC__`) these are contract-only stubs (`allocates`/`\\fresh`,
  `frees`/`\\freeable`), never proven; elsewhere they are `malloc` and `free`, with no null check.
- Model proof units (swdb.c_lowering): every vector and pair model function can be rebuilt from its C name alone and
  proven once with `swdb prove --model <name> --adapter wp`.
"""

import hashlib
import re
from pathlib import Path

MODELS_ID = "swdb-std-models"
MODELS_VERSION = "2"                 # bump on any change to a contract, a body or the struct layout
OUT_OF_RANGE = "std.vector.at.out_of_range"     # the failed-check name; the CBMC harness prints it for the C++ too
INDEX_PRECONDITION = "std.vector.operator_index.n_below_size"
VECTOR_MEMBERS = ("ctor", "ctor_count", "ctor_count_value", "copy_ctor", "move_ctor", "dtor", "operator_index", "at",
                  "data", "size", "empty", "begin", "end", "push_back", "resize", "reserve", "clear", "swap")
PAIR_MEMBERS = ("ctor_default", "ctor", "copy_ctor", "operator_assign")
ALLOCATING = {"ctor_count", "ctor_count_value", "copy_ctor", "push_back", "resize", "reserve"}
STANDARD = "ISO/IEC 14882:2017 (C++17)"
SENTENCE_LIBRARY = ("The pinned standard library (libc++ of clang {clang}) implements the modeled members of {types} as "
                    "the C++ standard ({standard}) says, as the model {model} states them.")
SENTENCE_ALLOCATION = "Allocation succeeds: every malloc (std::vector growth, new[]) returns usable memory, never null."


def identity(path=None):
    """{id, sha256} of the model version: the sha256 of this module's source (every contract, body and layout)."""
    source = Path(path) if path else Path(__file__)
    return {"id": f"{MODELS_ID}-{MODELS_VERSION}", "sha256": hashlib.sha256(source.read_bytes()).hexdigest()}


def assumptions(lowering, clang_version, lowering_tool):
    """The assumption entries a proof record of this C lowering adds (map 16 item 7): "the pinned standard library
    implements the modeled members as the standard says" (trusted tool; reference: the model version) when it uses a
    model, and "allocation succeeds" (trusted tool; reference: the model version, or the C lowering tool that lowers
    new[] to malloc) when it allocates. `lowering_tool`: {id, sha256} of the C lowering tool."""
    found = []
    model = identity()
    if lowering.std_models:
        types = ", ".join(lowering.std_models)
        found.append({"kind": "trusted_tool", "reference": dict(model),
                      "sentence": SENTENCE_LIBRARY.format(clang=clang_version, types=types, standard=STANDARD,
                                                          model=model["id"])})
    if lowering.allocation:
        found.append({"kind": "trusted_tool", "reference": dict(model if lowering.std_models else lowering_tool),
                      "sentence": SENTENCE_ALLOCATION})
    return found


def method_problem(method, lowering):
    """Why the method version does not admit this lowering's models (its `models.std_vector` / `models.std_pair`
    must be this model version), or None. A mismatch runs nothing, as for the translators."""
    found = identity()
    section = method.data.get("models") or {}
    for key, prefix in (("std_vector", "std_vector_"), ("std_pair", "std_pair_")):
        if not any(name.startswith(prefix) for name in lowering.std_models):
            continue
        pinned = section.get(key) if isinstance(section, dict) else None
        if not isinstance(pinned, dict) or {k: pinned.get(k) for k in ("id", "sha256")} != found:
            return (f"the C lowering uses the {key} model {found['id']} (sha256 {found['sha256'][:12]}...), but "
                    f"method version {method.id} pins models.{key} = {pinned}")
    return None


def pins(lowering):
    """The content-hash set's `std_models` pin ({id, sha256} of the model version) when the C uses a model."""
    return {"std_models": identity()} if lowering.std_models else {}


MACROS = """\
/* swdb-std-models: the model's two check hooks (CBMC and the native harness define them first). */
#ifndef SWDB_MODEL_REQUIRE
#define SWDB_MODEL_REQUIRE(c, name) ((void)0)
#endif
#ifndef SWDB_MODEL_FAIL
#define SWDB_MODEL_FAIL(name) abort()
#endif"""


def _max(t):
    """libc++'s max_size(): min(SIZE_MAX / sizeof(T), PTRDIFF_MAX), as C (and ACSL, whose annotations are preprocessed)."""
    return f"((size_t)PTRDIFF_MAX < SIZE_MAX / sizeof({t}) ? (size_t)PTRDIFF_MAX : SIZE_MAX / sizeof({t}))"


def _decl(t, name):
    return f"{t}{name}" if t.endswith("*") else f"{t} {name}"


def vector_struct_fields(t):
    return [f"{_decl(t + ' *', 'data')};", "size_t size;", "size_t capacity;"]


def vector_logic(v, t):
    """The validity predicate of one vector struct (ACSL only)."""
    return (f"/* swdb-std-models: the representation invariant of {v} (data, size, capacity). */\n"
            f"/*@ predicate {v}_valid({v} *v) =\n"
            f"      \\valid(v) && \\initialized(v) && v->size <= v->capacity && v->capacity <= {_max(t)} &&\n"
            f"      (v->capacity == 0 ? v->data == \\null : \\valid(v->data + (0 .. v->capacity - 1))) &&\n"
            f"      \\initialized(v->data + (0 .. v->size - 1));\n"
            f"    predicate {v}_readable({v} *v) =\n"
            f"      \\valid_read(v) && \\initialized(v) && v->size <= v->capacity &&\n"
            f"      (v->capacity == 0 ? v->data == \\null : \\valid(v->data + (0 .. v->capacity - 1))) &&\n"
            f"      \\initialized(v->data + (0 .. v->size - 1));\n*/")


def _mangle(t):
    return re.sub(r"\s+", "_", re.sub(r"\s*\*", " ptr", t.strip()))


def allocator(t):
    """[(C name, C text)] of the allocator models: their contracts are the "allocation succeeds" assumption (map 16
    item 7), so WP reads them and never proves them; CBMC and the native runs use malloc and free."""
    a = f"swdb_alloc_{_mangle(t)}"
    alloc = (f"/* swdb-std-models allocator (trusted: \"allocation succeeds\"): n fresh, valid elements. */\n"
             f"#ifdef __FRAMAC__\n"
             f"/*@ requires n >= 0;\n    assigns \\nothing;\n    allocates \\result;\n"
             f"    ensures \\fresh(\\result, n * sizeof({t})) && \\valid(\\result + (0 .. n - 1)); */\n"
             f"{_decl(t + ' *', a)}(size_t n);\n"
             f"#else\n"
             f"static inline {_decl(t + ' *', a)}(size_t n) {{ return ({t} *)malloc(n * sizeof({t})); }}\n"
             f"#endif")
    free = ("/* swdb-std-models deallocator (trusted with the allocator). */\n"
            "#ifdef __FRAMAC__\n"
            "/*@ requires p == \\null || \\freeable(p);\n    assigns \\nothing;\n    frees p; */\n"
            "void swdb_free(void *p);\n"
            "#else\n"
            "static inline void swdb_free(void *p) { free(p); }\n"
            "#endif")
    return [(a, alloc), ("swdb_free", free)]


def _helpers(v, t):
    """libc++'s growth policy (implementation-defined by the standard): __recommend and the reallocation step."""
    recommend = (
        f"/* swdb-std-models helper: libc++ __recommend (the capacity a growth to new_size asks for). The standard leaves\n"
        f"   the growth policy to the implementation ([vector.capacity] p1 note: capacity() >= size()). */\n"
        f"/*@ requires {v}_readable(this) && new_size <= {_max(t)};\n"
        f"    assigns \\nothing;\n"
        f"    ensures new_size <= \\result <= {_max(t)}; */\n"
        f"static size_t {v}_recommend(const {v} *this, size_t new_size) {{\n"
        f"  size_t ms = {_max(t)};\n"
        f"  if (this->capacity >= ms / 2) return ms;\n"
        f"  return 2 * this->capacity > new_size ? 2 * this->capacity : new_size;\n}}")
    grow = (
        f"/* swdb-std-models helper: reallocation to capacity cap (allocate, move the elements, free the old buffer). */\n"
        f"/*@ requires {v}_valid(this) && this->size <= cap && cap > this->capacity && cap <= {_max(t)};\n"
        f"    requires this->capacity == 0 || \\freeable(this->data);\n"
        f"    assigns *this;\n"
        f"    allocates this->data;\n"
        f"    frees this->data;\n"
        f"    ensures {v}_valid(this) && this->capacity == cap && this->size == \\old(this->size);\n"
        f"    ensures \\forall integer k; 0 <= k < this->size ==> this->data[k] == \\old(this->data[k]);\n"
        f"    ensures \\old(this->capacity) > 0 ==> !\\valid(\\old(this->data)); */\n"
        f"static void {v}_grow({v} *this, size_t cap) {{\n"
        f"  {_decl(t + ' *', 'fresh')} = swdb_alloc_{_mangle(t)}(cap);   /* allocation succeeds (assumption entry) */\n"
        f"  /*@ loop invariant 0 <= k <= this->size;\n"
        f"      loop invariant \\forall integer j; 0 <= j < k ==> fresh[j] == this->data[j];\n"
        f"      loop invariant \\initialized(fresh + (0 .. k - 1));\n"
        f"      loop assigns k, fresh[0 .. cap - 1];\n"
        f"      loop variant this->size - k; */\n"
        f"  for (size_t k = 0; k < this->size; ++k) fresh[k] = this->data[k];\n"
        f"  swdb_free(this->data);\n"
        f"  this->data = fresh;\n"
        f"  this->capacity = cap;\n}}")
    return recommend, grow


def vector_member(v, t, member):
    """[(C name, C text)] for one vector member: its helpers first, then the member itself."""
    m = _max(t)
    zero = f"({t})0"
    ref = f"{t} *" if not t.endswith("*") else f"{t}*"
    out = []
    if member in ALLOCATING or member == "dtor":
        out += allocator(t)
    if member in ("push_back", "resize", "reserve"):
        recommend, grow = _helpers(v, t)
        if member != "reserve":
            out.append((f"{v}_recommend", recommend))
        out.append((f"{v}_grow", grow))
    if member == "ctor":
        text = (f"/* [vector.cons] p1, [container.requirements.general] Table 83 (X u;): an empty vector. */\n"
                f"/*@ requires \\valid(this);\n    assigns *this;\n"
                f"    ensures {v}_valid(this) && this->size == 0; */\n"
                f"static void {v}_ctor({v} *this) {{ this->data = NULL; this->size = 0; this->capacity = 0; }}")
    elif member in ("ctor_count", "ctor_count_value"):
        value = member == "ctor_count_value"
        what = ("[vector.cons] p6-p7: vector(size_type n, const T& value): n copies of value." if value else
                "[vector.cons] p3-p4: explicit vector(size_type n): n value-initialized elements.")
        fill = "value" if value else zero
        params = f"{v} *this, size_t n" + (f", {_decl(t, 'value')}" if value else "")
        text = (f"/* {what} */\n"
                f"/*@ requires \\valid(this) && n <= {m};\n    assigns *this;\n    allocates this->data;\n"
                f"    ensures {v}_valid(this) && this->size == n;\n"
                f"    ensures \\forall integer k; 0 <= k < n ==> this->data[k] == {'value' if value else '0'}; */\n"
                f"static void {v}_{member}({params}) {{\n"
                f"  this->data = NULL; this->size = 0; this->capacity = 0;\n"
                f"  if (n == 0) return;\n"
                f"  this->data = swdb_alloc_{_mangle(t)}(n);   /* allocation succeeds (assumption entry) */\n"
                f"  this->capacity = n;\n"
                f"  /*@ loop invariant 0 <= k <= n;\n"
                f"      loop invariant \\forall integer j; 0 <= j < k ==> this->data[j] == {'value' if value else '0'};\n"
                f"      loop invariant \\initialized(this->data + (0 .. k - 1));\n"
                f"      loop assigns k, this->data[0 .. n - 1];\n      loop variant n - k; */\n"
                f"  for (size_t k = 0; k < n; ++k) this->data[k] = {fill};\n"
                f"  this->size = n;\n}}")
    elif member == "copy_ctor":
        text = (f"/* [container.requirements.general] Table 83 (X u(a);): u == a; [vector.cons]. */\n"
                f"/*@ requires \\valid(this) && {v}_readable(other) && \\separated(this, other);\n    assigns *this;\n"
                f"    allocates this->data;\n"
                f"    ensures {v}_valid(this) && this->size == other->size;\n"
                f"    ensures \\forall integer k; 0 <= k < other->size ==> this->data[k] == other->data[k]; */\n"
                f"static void {v}_copy_ctor({v} *this, const {v} *other) {{\n"
                f"  this->data = NULL; this->size = 0; this->capacity = 0;\n"
                f"  if (other->size == 0) return;\n"
                f"  this->data = swdb_alloc_{_mangle(t)}(other->size);   /* allocation succeeds (assumption entry) */\n"
                f"  this->capacity = other->size;\n"
                f"  /*@ loop invariant 0 <= k <= other->size;\n"
                f"      loop invariant \\forall integer j; 0 <= j < k ==> this->data[j] == other->data[j];\n"
                f"      loop invariant \\initialized(this->data + (0 .. k - 1));\n"
                f"      loop assigns k, this->data[0 .. other->size - 1];\n      loop variant other->size - k; */\n"
                f"  for (size_t k = 0; k < other->size; ++k) this->data[k] = other->data[k];\n"
                f"  this->size = other->size;\n}}")
    elif member == "move_ctor":
        text = (f"/* [container.requirements.general] Table 83 (X u(rv);): u holds rv's former value; rv is left valid. */\n"
                f"/*@ requires \\valid(this) && {v}_valid(other) && \\separated(this, other);\n"
                f"    assigns *this, *other;\n"
                f"    ensures {v}_valid(this) && {v}_valid(other);\n"
                f"    ensures this->data == \\old(other->data) && this->size == \\old(other->size); */\n"
                f"static void {v}_move_ctor({v} *this, {v} *other) {{\n"
                f"  *this = *other;\n  other->data = NULL; other->size = 0; other->capacity = 0;\n}}")
    elif member == "dtor":
        text = (f"/* [container.requirements.general] Table 83 (a.~X()): destroys the elements, frees all memory. */\n"
                f"/*@ requires {v}_valid(this) && (this->capacity == 0 || \\freeable(this->data));\n    assigns \\nothing;\n"

                f"    ensures \\old(this->capacity) > 0 ==> !\\valid(\\old(this->data)); */\n"

    elif member == "operator_index":
        text = (f"/* [sequence.reqmts] Table 88 (a[n]: *(a.begin() + n)); n < size() is the caller's obligation. */\n"
                f"/*@ requires {v}_readable(this) && n < this->size;\n    assigns \\nothing;\n"

                f"static {ref}{v}_operator_index(const {v} *this, size_t n) {{\n"

    elif member == "at":
        text = (f"/* [sequence.reqmts] Table 88 (a.at(n): *(a.begin() + n); throws out_of_range if n >= a.size()).\n"

                f"/*@ requires {v}_readable(this) && n < this->size;\n    assigns \\nothing;\n"

                f"static {ref}{v}_at(const {v} *this, size_t n) {{\n"

    elif member == "empty":

                f"    ensures \\result <==> this->size == 0; */\n"

                f"    ensures \\result == this->data + this->size; */\n"
                f"static {ref}{v}_end(const {v} *this) {{ return this->size == 0 ? this->data : this->data + this->size; }}")
    elif member == "push_back":
        text = (f"/* [vector.modifiers] p1: push_back(const T& x) appends x; it causes reallocation if the new size is\n"

                f"/*@ requires {v}_valid(this) && this->size < {m};\n"
                f"    assigns *this, this->data[this->size];\n    allocates this->data;\n    frees this->data;\n"

                f"            !\\valid(\\old(this->data)); */\n"
                f"static void {v}_push_back({v} *this, {_decl(t, 'x')}) {{\n"
                f"  if (this->size == this->capacity) {v}_grow(this, {v}_recommend(this, this->size + 1));\n"
                f"  this->data[this->size] = x;\n"
                f"  this->size += 1;\n}}")
    elif member == "resize":
        text = (f"/* [vector.capacity] p13-p15: resize(sz) erases the last size() - sz elements, or appends sz - size()\n"

                f"/*@ requires {v}_valid(this) && n <= {m};\n"

                f"    ensures {v}_valid(this) && this->size == n;\n"
                f"    ensures \\forall integer k; 0 <= k < n && k < \\old(this->size) ==> this->data[k] == \\old(this->data[k]);\n"
                f"    ensures \\forall integer k; \\old(this->size) <= k < n ==> this->data[k] == 0;\n"
                f"    ensures n <= \\old(this->capacity) ==> this->data == \\old(this->data);\n"
                f"    ensures n > \\old(this->capacity) && \\old(this->capacity) > 0 ==> !\\valid(\\old(this->data)); */\n"
                f"static void {v}_resize({v} *this, size_t n) {{\n"
                f"  if (n > this->capacity) {v}_grow(this, {v}_recommend(this, n));\n"
                f"  size_t k = this->size;\n"
                f"  /*@ loop invariant this->size <= k && (k <= n || k == this->size);\n"
                f"      loop invariant \\forall integer j; this->size <= j < k ==> this->data[j] == 0;\n"
                f"      loop invariant \\initialized(this->data + (0 .. k - 1));\n"
                f"      loop assigns k, this->data[this->size .. n - 1];\n      loop variant n - k; */\n"

                f"/*@ requires {v}_valid(this) && n <= {m};\n"
                f"    assigns *this;\n    allocates this->data;\n    frees this->data;\n"
                f"    ensures {v}_valid(this) && this->size == \\old(this->size) && this->capacity >= n;\n"
                f"    ensures \\forall integer k; 0 <= k < this->size ==> this->data[k] == \\old(this->data[k]);\n"
                f"    ensures n <= \\old(this->capacity) ==> this->data == \\old(this->data);\n"
                f"    ensures n > \\old(this->capacity) && \\old(this->capacity) > 0 ==> !\\valid(\\old(this->data)); */\n"
                f"static void {v}_reserve({v} *this, size_t n) {{\n"

        text = (f"/* [sequence.reqmts] Table 88 (a.clear(): destroys every element; a.empty() after). */\n"
                f"/*@ requires {v}_valid(this);\n    assigns this->size;\n"
                f"    ensures {v}_valid(this) && this->size == 0; */\n"
                f"static void {v}_clear({v} *this) {{ this->size = 0; }}")
    elif member == "swap":
        text = (f"/* [vector.special] p1, [container.requirements.general] Table 83 (a.swap(b): exchanges the contents;\n"
                f"   no iterator is invalidated). */\n"
                f"/*@ requires {v}_valid(this) && {v}_valid(other) && \\separated(this, other);\n"
                f"    assigns *this, *other;\n"
                f"    ensures this->data == \\old(other->data) && this->size == \\old(other->size);\n"

                f"    ensures {v}_valid(this) && {v}_valid(other); */\n"
                f"static void {v}_swap({v} *this, {v} *other) {{ {v} t = *this; *this = *other; *other = t; }}")

        raise KeyError(member)
    out.append((f"{v}_{member}", text))

def pair_member(p, a, b, member):
    """(C name, C text) of one pair member."""
    if member == "ctor_default":
        text = (f"/* [pairs.pair] p2-p3: pair(): value-initializes first and second. */\n"
                f"/*@ requires \\valid(this);\n    assigns *this;\n"
                f"    ensures this->first == 0 && this->second == 0; */\n"
                f"static void {p}_ctor_default({p} *this) {{ this->first = ({a})0; this->second = ({b})0; }}")
    elif member == "ctor":
        text = (f"/* [pairs.pair] p5-p11: pair(x, y): initializes first with x and second with y. */\n"
                f"/*@ requires \\valid(this);\n    assigns *this;\n"
                f"    ensures this->first == x && this->second == y; */\n"
                f"static void {p}_ctor({p} *this, {_decl(a, 'x')}, {_decl(b, 'y')}) {{ this->first = x; this->second = y; }}")
    elif member == "copy_ctor":
        text = (f"/* [pairs.pair] p2 (pair(const pair&) = default): copies first and second. */\n"
                f"/*@ requires \\valid(this) && \\valid_read(other) && \\initialized(other);\n    assigns *this;\n"
                f"    ensures this->first == \\old(other->first) && this->second == \\old(other->second); */\n"
                f"static void {p}_copy_ctor({p} *this, const {p} *other) {{ *this = *other; }}")
    elif member == "operator_assign":
        text = (f"/* [pairs.pair] p15-p17: operator=(const pair& p) assigns p.first to first and p.second to second;\n"
                f"   returns *this. */\n"
                f"/*@ requires \\valid(this) && \\valid_read(other) && \\initialized(other);\n    assigns *this;\n"
                f"    ensures this->first == \\old(other->first) && this->second == \\old(other->second);\n"
                f"    ensures \\result == this; */\n"
                f"static {p} *{p}_operator_assign({p} *this, const {p} *other) {{ *this = *other; return this; }}")
    else:
        raise KeyError(member)
    text = text.replace("    ensures ", "    ensures \\initialized(this);\n    ensures ", 1)
    return f"{p}_{member}", text

def _element(mangled):
    """The C element type whose mangled spelling is `mangled` (scalars and pointers to them), or None."""
    from swdb import c_lowering
    stars = 0
    while mangled.endswith("_ptr"):
        mangled, stars = mangled[:-4], stars + 1
    for name in sorted(c_lowering.INTEGER_TYPES | c_lowering.FLOAT_TYPES | set(c_lowering.INTERNAL_TYPES.values())):
        if _mangle(name) == mangled:
            return name + (" " + "*" * stars if stars else "")
    return None


def _vector_types(v, t):
    return (f"typedef struct {v} {v};\nstruct {v} {{ {' '.join(vector_struct_fields(t))} }};\n{MACROS}\n"
            f"{vector_logic(v, t)}")


def _vector_unit(match):
    v, member = match.group(1), match.group(2)
    t = _element(v[len("std_vector_"):])
    if t is None or t == "bool":
        return None
    head = [(f"{v}_types", _vector_types(v, t))]
    if member in ("recommend", "grow"):
        recommend, grow = _helpers(v, t)
        return head + (allocator(t) + [(f"{v}_grow", grow)] if member == "grow" else [(f"{v}_recommend", recommend)])
    return head + vector_member(v, t, member)


def _pair_unit(match):
    rest, member = match.group(1), match.group(2)
    words = rest.split("_")
    for cut in range(1, len(words)):
        a, b = _element("_".join(words[:cut])), _element("_".join(words[cut:]))
        if a and b:

def member_specs(member):
    if member.endswith('_ctor_count_value'):
        return constructor_specs()
    if member.endswith('_dtor'):
        return destructor_specs()
    if member.endswith('_reserve'):
        # The complete helper body is part of this public source unit. Every
        # induction duty is reproved here; no desired grow lemma is imported.
        return grow_specs() + reserve_specs()
    if member.endswith('_grow'):
        return grow_specs()
    raise ValueError('qualified member has no mapped source inventory')


def projection_parts(statement):
    """Exact conjunction/forall expansion; neither piece assumes the other."""
    quantifiers = (r'\forall Heap::heap h; \forall Heap::int_values values; '
                   r'\forall integer r,o,b,bo,s,c; ')
    antecedent = (r't25_repr(h,r,o,b,bo,s,c) && (s == 0 || r != b) && '
                  r'Heap::bounded_int_values(values,bo,s)')
    projected = 'Heap::project_int_region(h,values,b,bo,s)'
    representation = 't25_repr(' + projected + ',r,o,b,bo,s,c)'
    original = quantifiers + antecedent + ' ==> t25v3_repr(' + projected + ',r,o,b,bo,s,c)'
    if statement != original or re.search(r'\bj\b', quantifiers + antecedent + representation):
        raise ValueError('projection expansion requires the exact original formula and a fresh index')
    repr_definition = r'''predicate t25v3_repr(Heap::heap h, integer r, integer o, integer b, integer bo,
                         integer s, integer c) =
      t25_repr(h,r,o,b,bo,s,c) && Heap::int32_region(h,b,bo,s);'''
    region_definition = '''predicate int32_region (h:heap) (b offset count:int) =
    forall j:int. 0 <= j < count -> int32_at h b (offset+4*j)'''
    if PRELUDE.count(repr_definition) != 1:
        raise ValueError('the represented-heap conjunction definition changed')
    definitions = []
    for name, text in [('vector_reallocation_vcs.py', repr_definition),
                       ('heap_reallocation.mlw', region_definition)]:
        raw = (HERE/name).read_bytes()
        encoded = text.encode()
        begin = raw.index(encoded)
        definitions.append({'path':name, 'begin':begin, 'end':begin+len(encoded),
                            'sha256':hashlib.sha256(encoded).hexdigest(),
                            'container_sha256':hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()})
    parts = [('grow.entry.int_projection.repr', quantifiers + antecedent + ' ==> ' + representation),
             ('grow.entry.int_projection.cells', quantifiers + r'\forall integer j; ' + antecedent +
              r' && 0 <= j < s ==> Heap::int32_at(' + projected + ',b,bo+4*j)')]
    return parts, {'id':'grow.entry.int_projection', 'original_statement':original,
        'quantifiers':quantifiers, 'antecedent':antecedent, 'fresh_index':'j',
        'fresh_index_free_in_antecedent':False, 'fresh_index_bound_in_outer_quantifiers':False,
        'parts':[name for name,_ in parts], 'combination':'AND: both isolated pieces are required',
        'equivalence':'A implies (R and forall j: B implies I) iff (A implies R) and forall fresh j: (A and B) implies I',
        'definition_sources':definitions, 'premises_added':[], 'dependencies':[],
        'region_substitution':{'h':projected, 'b':'b', 'offset':'bo', 'count':'s', 'j':'j'},
        'reference_role':'original logical target only; never imported or launched as a proved result'}

                expanded, receipt = projection_parts(statement)
                reference = 'references/' + f'{index:03d}-t25v3_grow_entry_int_projection.c'
                files[reference] = lemma_source(name, statement).encode()
                receipt['reference'] = {'path':reference,'sha256':hashlib.sha256(files[reference]).hexdigest()}

def prepare(member, directory):
    """Emit an explicitly incomplete draft; no admission or result promotion."""
    plan, files = declaration(member)
    directory = Path(directory)
    directory.mkdir(exist_ok=False)
    for name, data in files.items():
        path = directory/name
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
        path.write_bytes(data)
    return plan


def check(member, directory):
    """Canonical source reconstruction, including the complete import directory.

    Matching self-declared hashes is insufficient. No caller can promote a
    prepared receipt to a proof or bypass pending semantic/source admission.
    """
    expected, files = declaration(member)
    directory = Path(directory)
    paths = list(directory.rglob('*'))
    if directory.is_symlink() or any(p.is_symlink() for p in paths):
        raise ValueError('a qualified packet or import path is symlinked')
    if any(not p.is_file() and not p.is_dir() for p in paths):
        raise ValueError('a qualified packet contains a special filesystem entry')
    actual = {str(p.relative_to(directory)) for p in paths if p.is_file()}
    directories = {str(p.relative_to(directory)) for p in paths if p.is_dir()}
    expected_dirs = {str(parent) for name in files for parent in Path(name).parents if str(parent) != '.'}
    if actual != set(files) or directories != expected_dirs:
        raise ValueError('the qualified source/packet/import membership changed')
    for name, data in files.items():
        if (directory/name).read_bytes() != data:
            raise ValueError('the canonical qualified source/VC declaration changed: ' + name)
    return expected
